title: Canonical Memory 持久化与所有权隔离
completed: V11 migration service/platform/persistence/src/main/resources/db/migration/V11__canonical_memory_lifecycle.sql: ALTER vc.memory_item adds conversation_id (FK->conversation ON DELETE CASCADE, for SESSION scope), deleted_at (soft delete), sets status default to PENDING_CONFIRMATION (catalog alphaModelCandidateInitialStatus), and adds a CHECK that SESSION scope requires a conversation binding.

Six SECURITY DEFINER lifecycle functions: create_memory_candidate (the ONLY model-output entry, inserts PENDING_CONFIRMATION candidates + a memory_evidence chain; Alpha scope SESSION/RELATIONSHIP only; SESSION requires conversation_id; verifies relationship/conversation ownership), confirm_memory_candidate (the sole PENDING_CONFIRMATION->ACCEPTED path, status-guarded, FOR UPDATE), reject_memory_candidate (->REJECTED), delete_memory (soft delete via deleted_at), list_memory (relationship-scoped, excludes deleted by default), get_memory.

Privilege revocation: REVOKE SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on memory_item and memory_evidence from every runtime role, so ALL memory access flows through the functions. This enforces INV-MEM-001 (model output only creates candidates; canonical ACCEPTED only via confirm) and cross-relationship list isolation (list_memory's relationship predicate cannot be bypassed by an owner-wide SELECT). FK CASCADE integrity is owner-scoped and unaffected.

SQL tests 32 (confirmation-only canonical path: candidate is PENDING_CONFIRMATION, confirm is the sole ACCEPTED path, direct INSERT by vc_api rejected insufficient_privilege), 33 (cross-user/cross-relationship-list/direct-access fail-closed), 34 (lifecycle + evidence chain + SESSION/RELATIONSHIP scope + soft delete + get excludes deleted). Full suite 01-34 PASS.

R1 PASS no P0/P1; confirmation-only path enforced via function gate + REVOKE of INSERT and UPDATE; cross-user/cross-relationship-list/missing-context fail-closed; independently re-run 34/34. Satisfies both acceptance criteria.

Java CanonicalMemoryRepository/Service wiring these SECURITY DEFINER functions and the OpenAPI surface for memory is a separate runtime-implementation card.

Optional hardening deferred (P3c): a CHECK (status IN candidate-statuses) would structurally backstop the confirmation-only invariant against a future function bug; P3b: validate conversation ownership for RELATIONSHIP scope when a conversation_id is supplied.
knownRisks: P2: point-ops get_memory/confirm_memory_candidate/reject_memory_candidate/delete_memory are owner-scoped (owner, memory_id) without a relationship_id predicate, so an owner can operate on their own memory across relationships. This is same-owner own-data access (no cross-tenant leak), consistent with the owner-based FORCE RLS model; list_memory (the primary read API) is relationship-scoped. If strict relationship-scoped point-ops are later required, add p_relationship_id + a predicate or a relationship-context GUC/RLS policy.

P3a: test 32 covers direct INSERT rejection but not direct UPDATE (REVOKE blocks UPDATE too, independently probed). P3b: a RELATIONSHIP candidate may bind another relationship's conversation (same owner). P3c: no CHECK on the status column allowed values.

Direct table access is fully revoked for runtime roles, so any future ad-hoc diagnostic read of memory_item/memory_evidence must use a SECURITY DEFINER function or a BYPASSRLS principal (never a runtime role).
